claim_text: FinanceQuery.run absolute query deadlines: setup and monitor scheduling must not renew the timeout; respect parent synthesis reserve; preserve cancellation vs timeout; reject late SQL/fetch/close success and clean up connections; investigate regressions and uncovered deadline/cancellation edges.
verdict_rationale: Independent immutable probes (source FQ-explore/delivery, executed unchanged under OS sandbox in FQ-execute) passed 4/4 on the candidate, dynamically verifying the core deadline/cancellation observables: setup cannot renew the bounded grant, the parent synthesis reserve shrinks the child grant, late SQL success after a timeout interrupt is rejected, cancellation takes precedence over late setup success at the observable level, and connections are always closed exactly once; the positive control functioned and is classified probe_bug. However, several declared subclaims were not executed (upfront nearly-exhausted no-connect rejection, late fetch success with populated rows, late-close-success rejection, fetch-loop cancellation, byte-limit remap, isolated monitor-recorded cancellation mapping), author evidence spans two separate runs (original collection BLOCKED_PROBE; a later passing recheck that adds no independent coverage), and an immutable historical replay shows host/revision sensitivity of exactly these probes. Only part of the claim was tested dynamically, so PASS_WITH_LIMITS rather than PASS.
verified_subclaims: Setup must not renew the timeout: the grant is fixed once via deadline.bounded_stage(self._limits.timeout) at finance_query.py L2209 before connection setup and monitor scheduling; a 0.4s connect inside a ~0.2s grant yields FinanceQueryTimedOut with zero execute calls and zero interrupts (expiry caught at the post-connect check L2222-2223, before monitor scheduling), and exactly one close (verified dynamically, probe test_setup_and_synthesis_reserve_cannot_renew_deadline). Note: this verifies expiry-at-setup rejection after connect; it does not exercise the upfront remaining() <= 0.001 no-connect rejection at L2210-2211.

Parent synthesis reserve is respected: ResearchDeadline.bounded_stage (research_contract.py L393-401) intersects the child grant with parent.expires_at - synthesis_reserve and the child carries no reserve of its own; the probe sanity assertion 0.0 < parent.stage_timeout(8.0) <= 0.25 held, and the ~0.2s effective grant caused the setup timeout despite limits.timeout=8.0 (verified dynamically).

Late SQL success after a timeout interrupt is rejected: execute() blocked on an Event released only by interrupt(); after the monitor interrupted and the SQL then 'succeeded' returning a cursor, FinanceQueryTimedOut was still raised; execute_calls == 1, interrupt_calls >= 1, close_calls == 1 (finance_query.py L2225-2279; verified dynamically, probe test_late_sql_success_after_timeout_interrupt_is_rejected).

Cancellation beats late setup success (outcome level): is_cancelled returning False for the first three invocations and True on the fourth yields FinanceQueryCancelled with no SQL executed and exactly one close (finance_query.py L2216-2245; verified dynamically, probe test_cancellation_beats_late_setup_success). The probe does not record whether the fourth invocation was evaluated in the monitor thread or a main-thread check, so the result is asserted at the observable level (exception type, zero execute calls, one close) and not pinned to a specific check site.

Connections are cleaned up: connection.close() was called exactly once in every scenario (control, deadline-exhausted setup, late-SQL timeout, cancelled) via the unconditional outer finally at finance_query.py L2282-2285, with stop_monitor always set (verified dynamically in all four probes).

Control happy path: the empty-result query returns a FinanceQueryResult with rows == (), audit.row_count == 0, exactly one execute, zero interrupts, one close (verified dynamically, probe test_control_happy_path_returns_result_and_closes).
not_verified_subclaims: Upfront nearly-exhausted grant rejection: the remaining() <= 0.001 check at finance_query.py L2210-2211 that raises before connect was NOT dynamically exercised; the setup probe performed one connect and one close before expiring, so it must not be counted as an upfront-no-connect test (static observation only).

Late fetch-loop success after an interrupt with populated rows: all adversarial probes used an empty cursor (fetchmany -> []), so _fetch_rows (finance_query.py L2380-2424) returning rows post-interrupt was not exercised; only the empty-cursor post-interrupt rejection at L2276-2279 was verified.

Late close success rejection: the source checks query_deadline.expired only AFTER connection.close() in the outer finally (finance_query.py L2287 vs L2282-2285); close() itself is unconditional and its return is not gated on deadline state. No dynamic probe isolated delayed/late-close-success semantics; the static L2287 check must not be conflated with dynamic coverage, and the passing author recheck does not increase independent coverage.

Pure monitor-recorded 'cancelled' -> FinanceQueryCancelled mapping (L2227-2230 marker deciding L2262-2264 / L2276-2278) was not isolated: the cancellation probe did not record which thread/check raised; the resulting exception type is identical either way.
Fetch-loop cancellation between fetchmany batches (finance_query.py L2391-2392).
Byte-limit path FinanceQueryLimitExceeded (finance_query.py L2416-2417) and the monitor-priority remap of structured fetch-loop errors to TimedOut/Cancelled in the except block (L2261-2267).
No-preemption boundary: a connect() that blocks forever still blocks run() (explicitly out of scope per packet; only deadline accounting was verified, not unblocking).
Real DuckDB interrupt()/close-under-interrupt semantics and connect latencies: probes used an in-memory fake connection gated on a threading.Event.
Monitor-thread lifecycle when interrupt() blocks (join timeout 0.2s, daemon thread) - potential thread leak untested.

Author-side claims: the original author-suite execution was blocked at collection (BLOCKED_PROBE, sandbox PermissionError); the separate later recheck (151 passed under an adjusted sandbox profile) is a distinct run on the same clean candidate, was not reviewed for claim coverage, and adds no independent coverage; author test assertions remain not_verified by this reviewer.
dataset_max_date swallowing FinanceQueryError, reverse_after_fetch, and _rows_to_evidence content hashing: untested.

findings.trigger: Parent ResearchDeadline.from_timeout(5.0, synthesis_reserve=4.8) with limits.timeout=8.0 gives a bounded_stage grant of ~0.2s; the injected connect sleeps 0.4s before returning.
findings.actual: FinanceQueryTimedOut raised; execute_calls == [] (no late SQL after setup), interrupt_calls == 0 (expiry caught at the post-connect check L2222-2223, before monitor scheduling), close_calls == 1. Setup consumed the absolute grant and did not renew it. This does not dynamically exercise the upfront remaining() <= 0.001 rejection at L2210-2211.

findings.trigger: bounded_stage(8.0) under a parent with a 4.8s synthesis reserve inside a 5.0s window; sanity assertion 0.0 < stage_timeout(8.0) <= 0.25.
findings.actual: Assertion held; child grant expires_at = min(parent.expires_at - synthesis_reserve, now + limit), i.e. the reserve is subtracted and the child carries no reserve of its own; the shrunken grant drove the setup timeout in the run-level probe.

findings.trigger: execute() blocks on a threading.Event released only by interrupt(); grant 0.5s; the monitor interrupts at expiry, then the SQL 'succeeds' and returns an empty cursor.
findings.actual: FinanceQueryTimedOut raised despite post-interrupt SQL success; execute_calls == 1, interrupt_calls >= 1, close_calls == 1. Late SQL success rejected via interrupted_for[0] == 'timeout'.

findings.trigger: is_cancelled returns False for the first three invocations and True on the fourth.
findings.actual: FinanceQueryCancelled raised; execute_calls == []; close_calls == 1. Cancellation beats late setup success at the observable level; the probe did not record whether the fourth invocation was consumed by the monitor thread or a main-thread check, so the outcome is not pinned to a specific check site.

findings.trigger: All four probe scenarios (happy path, deadline-exhausted setup, late-SQL timeout, cancellation).
findings.actual: connection.close() called exactly once in every scenario and stop_monitor always set; unconditional cleanup in the outer finally.

findings.trigger: Static reading of the upfront grant check.
findings.actual: remaining() <= 0.001 raises FinanceQueryTimedOut before connect; not exercised dynamically (the setup probe performed one connect and one close before expiring), so the upfront-no-connect path remains unverified.

findings.trigger: Static reading of the final expiry check relative to cleanup.
findings.actual: query_deadline.expired is checked only after the outer finally has already closed the connection, rejecting success landing after the last in-loop check; this is distinct from any delayed-close-success probe, which was never run. Passing author recheck tests do not add independent coverage here.

findings.trigger: Static analysis of monitor loop wait granularity.
findings.actual: stop_monitor.wait(min(0.01, query_deadline.remaining())) polls cancellation/expiry at <=10ms cadence; interrupt latency verified only indirectly via the event-gated late-SQL probe, not as a hard bound.

findings.trigger: Static analysis of except-mapping priority when the monitor recorded a cause.
findings.actual: The first interrupted_for marker remaps any exception, including a fetch-loop FinanceQueryLimitExceeded or fetch-loop Cancelled, to TimedOut/Cancelled; cause priority belongs to the monitor marker. Not observed dynamically (empty cursor), so the byte-limit remap interaction is unverified.

limitations: Only part of the FQ claim was tested dynamically: the upfront remaining() <= 0.001 no-connect rejection (L2210-2211), late fetch-loop success with populated rows, late-close-success rejection semantics (the L2287 post-close expiry check is static only), fetch-loop cancellation, the byte-limit remap interaction, and the isolated monitor-recorded cancellation mapping were not executed. Hence PASS_WITH_LIMITS, not PASS.

Author evidence consists of two separate runs, not one uninterrupted execution: the original collection was BLOCKED_PROBE (sandbox PermissionError on candidate/intelligence/users; 0 tests executed), and a later recheck under an adjusted profile (metadata stat permitted on that directory only, contents still denied) passed 151/151 on the same clean candidate. The recheck adds no independent coverage, and the author tests were not reviewed for claim coverage.

Probes used an in-memory fake connection (execute/fetchmany/interrupt/close) with event-gated interrupt ordering; real DuckDB interrupt(), close-under-interrupt, and connect latencies were not exercised. No production database, network, or model calls were made.

The cancellation probe asserts outcome-level observables only (exception type, zero executes, one close); it does not record which thread or check site consumed the fourth cancelled() invocation, so behavior is not pinned to a specific check.

Adversarial probes 1 and 2 depend on real host scheduling: margins are generous (~0.2s grant vs 0.4s connect; 0.5s grant with a 5s event-gate safety and <=10ms monitor polling), but under extreme load the sanity bound stage_timeout(8.0) <= 0.25 or the gate timeout could in principle flake.

The immutable historical replay (2 failures / 2 passes at revision 50330cf4) shows these probes and the underlying check placements are sensitive to revision/host timing; this is sensitivity evidence only, and the root cause of historical wall-clock failures is neither investigated nor inferred, per packet constraints.
No claim is made about forcibly preempting connect()/close() or about hard real-time OS scheduling (explicitly out of scope per packet).
Findings are scoped to the FQ claim only; this is not a full-repo review and implies no production acceptance or authorization.
